_tier_map_note: resolveClaudeModel/resolveCodexModel read tier->model from review-model-tiers.json, not from `vendors` below. The two agree today and CI verifies both against the same provider docs; `vendors` here is the documented policy and the tier map is the runtime lookup.
_runtime_status_note: Read at runtime by src/lib/review-strategy.ts. The runner classifies each PR from the cloned working copy and folds the result into the quality config the reviewers receive; the version, class, and tier are stamped into every annotation.
_comment: Single source of truth for how crosscheck picks a model, effort, and step set. Every review comment cites `version` so a past review can be explained by the policy in force when it ran. Supersedes review-model-tiers.json, which is retained for backwards compat. Re-verify every review_interval_days with `npm run verify:strategy`.

swe_bench_verified.measures: Resolving real GitHub issues in Python repositories. Backend/general proxy only.
swe_bench_verified.caveat: Comparable within one leaderboard run. Cross-leaderboard positions are indicative only.

frontend_code_arena.measures: Blind pairwise human preference on generated frontend output: visual fidelity, interaction design, function.
frontend_code_arena.caveat: Measures generation, not defect detection. Claude Opus 5 is absent from the retrieved leaderboard - a missing measurement, not a low score.

banned_models.reason: Banned from code review on cost. $50/MTok output is 2x claude-opus-5 for a LOWER SWE-bench Verified score (95.0 vs 96.0). At the measured 48k output tokens per review that is $2.40 a call with no capability justification.

codex._min_cli_version_note: gpt-5.6-* return HTTP 400 'requires a newer version of Codex' below this. The CLI accepts --model under subscription auth; the old auth!=api-key guard in resolveCodexModel was wrong and dropped the configured model.

domains._comment: Capability is domain-shaped, not scalar. claude-opus-5 leads backend defect resolution; kimi-k3 leads frontend. A single tier ladder cannot express that. Detected from changed-file extensions; `mixed` and `unknown` both fall back to `backend`, the conservative default.

frontend.threshold: more frontend files than backend files
frontend.basis: Frontend Code Arena Elo: kimi-k3 1679 > gpt-5.6-sol 1618 > glm-5.2 1587. Falls back to installed vendors when opencode is unavailable.
frontend.confidence: hypothesis - the benchmark measures generation, not review. Pending local A/B.

backend.basis: SWE-bench Verified: claude-opus-5 0.960 > claude-sonnet-5 0.852 > deepseek-v4-pro 0.806 > claude-haiku-4-5 0.733.

_pr_classes_note: ORDER IS THE ROUTING LOGIC - first match wins. `risky` sits second, immediately after `generated`, so consequence-based promotion dominates every cheapening rule below it: a deletion-only PR that removes auth code, or a 2-file change to a migration, must not fall through to `fast`.

pr_classes.label: Generated / vendored only
pr_classes.reason: every changed file is generated or vendored - nothing here is human-authored

pr_classes.label: Security / data-critical
pr_classes._any_path_matches_note: Anchored on path segments and extensions. Unanchored, `auth` matched author/authors/oauth and `migration` matched MIGRATION_AND_GROWTH.md, promoting a pure-docs PR to thorough with a full fix/recheck loop.
pr_classes.reason: touches a security or data-critical path, where a missed defect is expensive - promoted on consequence, not on predicted difficulty

pr_classes.label: Deletion-only
pr_classes.focus: dangling references only: imports, call sites, config keys, route registrations, docs pointing at removed symbols
pr_classes.reason: removal-only, so the risk is reference breakage rather than defect density; a wrong deletion is reverted, not patched

pr_classes.label: Documentation / specification
pr_classes.focus: internal contradiction, claims contradicted by the code the doc describes, stale cross-references
pr_classes.reason: specification review is open-ended design negotiation, which no automated fix loop terminates - review only

pr_classes.label: Test-only
pr_classes.focus: assertions that cannot fail, over-mocking that voids the test, coverage claimed but not exercised
pr_classes.reason: tests only - no production code path changes

pr_classes.label: Config / infrastructure
pr_classes.focus: secrets in plaintext, permission widening, resource limits, deploy-order breakage
pr_classes.reason: low defect density but high blast radius - cheap to review, expensive to get wrong

pr_classes.label: Trivial
pr_classes.reason: small and low-risk, and PRs this size merge in minutes - latency matters more than depth

pr_classes.label: Standard code
pr_classes.reason: default class - no narrower rule matched

ladder._comment: Escalate on measured non-convergence, never on predicted complexity. Scope narrows each round; the model never weakens. Where a model exposes no effort levels, the effort step degrades to a model step (see effort_fallback).

cross_vendor.strength: An independent second perspective. A vendor switch broke a stalled loop twice in the census (PR #2057, #2060) after same-vendor escalation had failed for 3-6 rounds.

single_vendor.strength: One CLI to authenticate, version, and monitor. No routing logic.
single_vendor.round_3_lever: raise effort, then promote one tier - no fresh-eyes option exists

conflict_resolve.reason: mechanical text surgery bounded by conflict markers - measured at 37s against ~643s for a review

citation._comment: Every crosscheck comment states the strategy it ran under, so a past review can be explained by the policy in force at the time.
citation.annotation_example: <!-- crosscheck: origin=claude reviewer=claude model=claude-opus-5 type=review round=1 verdict=BLOCK service=crosscheck sha=abc123 strategy=1.0.0 class=risky tier=thorough -->
citation.body_example: _Reviewed with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) via [Crosscheck](https://github.com/humanbased-ai/crosscheck) with Opus 5 (high) — thorough tier · touches a security or data-critical path, where a missed defect is expensive · strategy v1.0.0_
